questions.question: The atomic number of an element is the number of
options: protons and neutrons in its nucleus
questions.explanation: Atomic number counts protons; protons plus neutrons gives the mass number.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Isotopes of an element have the same
options: mass number but different atomic numbers
number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ only in neutron count, so the atomic number is unchanged.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What is the electron configuration of sodium (atomic number 11)?
questions.explanation: Eleven electrons fill 1s², 2s², 2p⁶ and leave one in 3s.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: How many moles are present in 22 g of carbon(IV) oxide? [C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO₂ = 44 g/mol, so moles = 22/44 = 0.5 mol.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: How many molecules are contained in 0.5 mole of a gas? [Avogadro's constant = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹]
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What amount of gas occupies 11.2 dm³ at s.t.p.? [molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³]
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: A compound contains 40% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Dividing by molar masses gives 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33, which simplifies to 1 : 2 : 1.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: For the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, what mass of oxygen is required to burn 4 g of hydrogen completely? [H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: 4 g of H₂ is 2 mol, which reacts with 1 mol of O₂, that is 32 g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following compounds contains ionic bonding?
questions.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following molecules contains only covalent bonds?
questions.explanation: Carbon shares electrons with four hydrogen atoms; the others are ionic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The bond formed when a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen is donated to a hydrogen ion to form NH₄⁺ is
questions.explanation: Both shared electrons come from one atom, which defines a dative (coordinate) bond.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃. [N = 14, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 80; nitrogen contributes 28, so 28/80 × 100 = 35%.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Across a period in the periodic table, the atomic radius of the elements generally
questions.explanation: Nuclear charge rises while the number of shells stays the same, pulling electrons closer.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The elements of Group 1 of the periodic table are known as
questions.explanation: Group 1 metals form strongly alkaline hydroxides in water.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The noble gases are chemically unreactive because
options: their outermost shells are completely filled
they have very high melting points
questions.explanation: A full outer shell leaves no tendency to gain, lose or share electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid is a substance that
questions.explanation: A Brønsted-Lowry acid is a proton donor; a base is a proton acceptor.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What is the pH of a solution whose hydrogen ion concentration is 1 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³?
questions.explanation: pH = −log[H⁺] = −log(10⁻³) = 3.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water is called
questions.explanation: H⁺ and OH⁻ combine to form water, leaving the salt in solution.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is an acid salt?
questions.explanation: It still contains a replaceable hydrogen atom from the parent acid.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What colour does phenolphthalein show in an alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acid and pink in alkali.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What volume of 0.05 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid is required to neutralise 25 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide?
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 0.0025; the reaction is 1:1, so volume = 0.0025/0.05 = 0.05 dm³ = 50 cm³.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Oxidation is best defined as the
questions.explanation: In electronic terms oxidation is electron loss and reduction is electron gain.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What is the oxidation number of sulphur in H₂SO₄?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: During the electrolysis of an electrolyte, cations migrate towards the
questions.explanation: Cations are positive, so they move to the negative electrode, the cathode.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What mass of copper is deposited when 2 faradays of electricity are passed through copper(II) sulphate solution? [Cu = 64]
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, so 2 faradays deposit 1 mole of copper, that is 64 g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-electrolyte?
questions.explanation: Sugar dissolves as neutral molecules, so there are no free ions to carry current.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: An increase in temperature increases the rate of a chemical reaction mainly because
options: the activation energy of the reaction is lowered
the particles collide more frequently and with greater energy
the concentration of the reactants increases
questions.explanation: Heating raises the proportion of collisions with energy above the activation energy.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by
options: being used up in the reaction
providing an alternative path of lower activation energy
increasing the temperature of the reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst is recovered unchanged in mass and does not move the equilibrium position.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: In the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), an increase in pressure favours
questions.explanation: The forward reaction reduces the number of gas molecules from 4 to 2, relieving the pressure.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: In an exothermic reaction, the enthalpy change ΔH is
options: always equal to the activation energy
questions.explanation: Heat is given out, so the products have less enthalpy than the reactants.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Temporary hardness in water is best removed by
questions.explanation: Boiling decomposes the dissolved hydrogencarbonates, which precipitate out.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The 5H₂O in the formula CuSO₄·5H₂O is referred to as
questions.explanation: It is water chemically combined in fixed proportion within the crystal.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: A gas occupies 300 cm³ at 27 °C. What volume will it occupy at 127 °C if the pressure is kept constant?
questions.explanation: By Charles' law, V₂ = 300 × 400/300 = 400 cm³, using temperatures in kelvin.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Graham's law states that the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the
questions.explanation: Lighter gases diffuse faster, in proportion to 1/√density.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which gas turns lime water milky?
questions.explanation: Insoluble calcium carbonate is precipitated, giving the milky appearance.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which gas relights a glowing splint?
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion, so the glowing splint bursts back into flame.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which gas burns with a characteristic 'pop' when a lighted splint is applied?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen explodes quietly with air, producing the familiar pop.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which gas turns damp red litmus paper blue?
questions.explanation: Ammonia dissolves to give an alkaline solution.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper because, in the presence of water, it acts as
questions.explanation: Chlorine and water form hypochlorous acid, which oxidises and so bleaches the dye.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: In the blast furnace, iron(III) oxide is reduced principally by
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide formed from coke removes oxygen from the ore.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The rusting of iron requires the presence of
questions.explanation: Both are necessary; iron does not rust in dry air or in air-free water.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Coating iron with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting is known as
questions.explanation: The more reactive zinc corrodes in place of the iron, protecting it sacrificially.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated, so each carbon carries the maximum number of hydrogens.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which observation distinguishes an alkene from an alkane?
options: It burns with a sooty flame
It is a gas at room temperature
questions.explanation: The double bond adds bromine across it, discharging the orange colour.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: What is the functional group of the alkanols?
questions.explanation: Alkanols (alcohols) carry the hydroxyl group.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The reaction between an alkanol and an alkanoic acid to produce a sweet-smelling compound and water is called
questions.explanation: The product is an ester, and the reaction is catalysed by concentrated sulphuric acid.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The conversion of ethene to polyethene is an example of
questions.explanation: The monomers join across their double bonds with no small molecule eliminated.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Soap is produced by the hydrolysis of fats and oils with an alkali. This process is called
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis of the ester links in the fat gives soap and glycerol.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is a condensation polymer?
questions.explanation: Nylon forms with the loss of water molecules at each link; the others are addition polymers.
questions.subject: Chemistry
